<!--
Write for the reviewer, not a changelog: lead with why, and let the diff carry the details.
Scale it to the change: a small PR needs only a line or two per heading.
Write under each heading; these comments do not render.
Add "## Risk / what to review" (non-obvious logic, edge cases, a frozen surface, areas you are less sure of)
or "## Deferred" (intentionally out of scope; link the follow-up) as their own headings only when they carry weight.
Link the issue, e.g. "Closes #123". Before you open the PR, run the checks in CONTRIBUTING.md.
Public-facing PR bodies, commits, docs, code comments, schema text, and branch names should state the reasoning in plain words rather than citing internal reference numbers.
-->

## Why

<!-- The problem or motivation: what was wrong, missing, or worth changing. -->

## What changed

<!-- A high-level summary, grouped by concern. The diff carries the line-by-line. -->

## Test plan

<!-- What you ran and the result (tests, the CONTRIBUTING.md checks, any manual run), or why testing does not apply. -->
